newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N.'s Annan goes to South Africa, Angola, Namibia.
newsitem.headline: U.N.'s Annan goes to South Africa, Angola, Namibia.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan plans a trip next week to South Africa, Angola, Namibia and Togo where the Organisation of African Unity is holding a summit later this month.
Spokesman Fred Eckhard said he would leave on Tuesday for Cape Town, Pretoria and Johannesburg and meet President Nelson Mandela as well as other South African officials.

On March 22, he travels to Namibia for a six-hour visit. He then goes for three days to Angola where the United Nations has its peacekeeping mission of more than 6,000 troops -- and where the government is helping Zairean rebels while the opposition UNITA is said to have ties with the Zairean government.

Annan, a native of Ghana, plans to attend the OAU summit in Lome on March 25 before returning to New York on March 28, Eckhard said. It is his first visit to Africa since becoming secretary-general on Jan. 1.
